lines.text: How did ten days vanish from history?

lines.text: In 1582, much of Catholic Europe went to bed on Thursday, October fourth, and woke up on Friday the fifteenth.

lines.text: The culprit: Julius Caesar's calendar, sixteen centuries old.

lines.text: A leap day every four years made its average year three hundred sixty-five and a quarter days.

lines.text: But Earth returns to the equinox about eleven minutes sooner.

lines.text: Eleven minutes a year doesn't sound like much.

lines.text: But it adds up to a whole day every hundred and twenty-eight years.

lines.text: By 1582 it had slipped ten days, and Easter was drifting away from the real equinox.

lines.text: So Pope Gregory the Thirteenth simply deleted them.
